Session 03 · M02 · Data quality, distributions & descriptive evidence

Read the shape of the evidence

Audit records, compare center and spread, and explore how unusual observations change a summary.

Before class

Readiness check

Three questions, one minute. Your score suggests a path through the lesson.

Take the check
1. One valid delivery time rises from 26 to 80 minutes. Which changes more?

The middle sorted value stays 22 minutes.

Correct. The mean uses the changed magnitude; the middle value remains 22.

The sum increases, so the mean increases.

2. An observation lies beyond an IQR fence. What does that establish?

An unusual value may be real. A flag is not proof of error.

Correct. Check provenance and plausibility, then explain any treatment.

Replacement requires a defensible reason, beyond a flag.

3. Group A has a larger average than Group B in an extract. Can you infer causation?

An average is descriptive. Study design governs causal interpretation.

Visual separation does not resolve confounding or selection.

Correct. State the observed difference and design limits.
